html:
SMTO-SKL-0168 — SMTO couldn't find that GitHub issue

GUID: 93736231-ad9d-5c07-877b-9674a42590bd
Slug: github-issue-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: github

What happened

  • GitHub says the issue, or something attached to it, isn't in this repository. GitHub also says this when your token isn't allowed to see it. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the issue on github.com and check its number and which repository it's in, then repeat your request with that repository and number. Issue numbers belong to one repository, so the same number in another repository is a different issue.
  2. On github.com, check that your token has read access to Issues (or Pull requests) for this repository. GitHub hides issues a token can't read, so they look missing.
  3. If you changed the token's permissions, update the granted permissions in your GitHub account entry in Parameter Store and select Save. SMTO checks the permissions recorded there before contacting GitHub.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the issue's title and details when you ask about it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't assume the issue was deleted; it may only be hidden from your token.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An issue operation (including related comment or issue resources) received HTTP 404 from GitHub in the resolved repository; GitHub may return 404 for inaccessible private resources.

What this means

  • An issue-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404, including related issue resources reached by that operation. This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.

Why this can happen

  • An issue-prefixed operation receives HTTP 404, including related issue resources reached by that operation.

How to diagnose it

  • Verify the exact issue-related route and permission; 404 may mean inaccessible.

How to fix it

  • GitHubService.dispatch maps 404 for issue* operations to issue_not_found with may_be_inaccessible=true. Verify the issue number exists in the exact owner/repo, and that the PAT has issues:read (or pull_requests:read for PR-backed issue comments) for that repository; 404 does not prove absence.
  • Verify the issue number in the exact repository and the Issues or Pull requests read permission; 404 can mean inaccessible.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A same-repository authorized read resolves the intended issue resource.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This diagnostic adds no GitHub access. Inspect the original receipt and request stage before repeating work; preserve exact account, host, repository and object identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
